title: Base Types
$comment: Base types, one file each under `data_types/base/`: how the platform stores a value — its size, its encoding and its C declaration. One kind, `base_type`, which a `value_type` names as its `base` and which no data element, argument, record field or array element names. The directory is mandatory and may be empty.

name.description: The type's identity; the file is named from it (`data_types/base/{name}.yaml`, or a suffixed name when another file collides case-insensitively) and is never what identifies it. Unique across the base types, must not be blank, and immutable.

kind.description: Always `base_type`. The layer holds one kind and is not discriminated; the field is an ordinary literal, kept, immutable as it was, so a base type file reads as it did when base types were a kind of the data types layer.

size.description: The size of the base type, in bits. Must be > 0. (unit: bits)

encoding.description: A required AUTOSAR BASE-TYPE-ENCODING token (NONE, 2C, IEEE754, ...); must not be blank, because a blank one is not round-trippable through the ARXML importer.

native_declaration.description: The C type name the generated code declares for this base type (for example `uint8_t`), emitted exactly as written as its `NATIVE-DECLARATION`. Required by check-model: SWCraft never derives one, so a base type without it still loads, but check-model reports it and ARXML generation refuses it until it is filled in.

description.description: Free text about the type. Written into the generated ARXML as the element's `DESC`, exactly as held; the empty default writes none.

package.description: The one sub-package of `/DataTypes/Base`, its layer's package, this base type is emitted in, a single SHORT-NAME segment: the base type and every reference to it take `/DataTypes/Base/{package}/`. Absent means `/DataTypes/Base` itself. SWCraft's importers record it for an element whose source path is exactly `/DataTypes/Base/{package}/{name}`, SWCraft's own layout, so a project's export imports back placed; and for an element that would otherwise share `/DataTypes/Base` with a name differing from its own only in case. An author may set it to place an element or to resolve such a collision. It is held to the AUTOSAR Identifier rule.
